[b]To Dance:[/b]

Come now, the position of the world is a fragile one, anti-Imperialism is on the rise once more, and the anti-christ and false prophet are presentthere is no doubt that we are entering the end of the days, The speaker was Radovna Melchjyonék, duchess of Montesque and the wife of the chief consul of Rosenmarkke, Consantin Alexandrii-Porgyros IV. It was with this rapid speech with which she had laid upon the poor second consul Phillipe Belgarde, Duke of Belgarde and Lower Montfleur. 

Madame, I do not know what you mean with such talk, it is truly nonsense, replied the duke, most certainly uncertain on how to proceed any further, and shocked at the suddenness by which the conversation had been thrown upon him. Nevertheless as he finished speaking he took the hand of the delicate Radovna and kissed it in greeting.

Come now, let us talk of other things, how are you doing? I daresay this is one of the finest parties you have thrown yet, stated the duke, releasing her hand.

Oh well I [i]suppose[/i] it is alright, though I daresay the third consul, the honourable Strømm, has been well known for her knack at hostingalark! I do believe she is due to arrive soon, replied deflecting the dukes praise and rising suddenly from the small cushioned stool she had been seated on, the folds of her skirts rustling slightly as she craned her neck ever so slightly to peer at the doors of the drawing room which remained shut.

Is she? enquired the duke, turning towards the doors ever so slightly, his view blocked by a chatting couple.

Oh yes, she made letter to me earlier informing me politely that she was to be present, you know she is the fiercest opponent of the anti-christ, that state the Neue Republik, replied Radovna, settling once more.

Yes, I had heard, replied the duke dryly, fully aware of Strømms vocalised and controversial takes on the largest hochdeutsche state on Erene, the Neue Republik.

You are a consul, are you not? enquired Radovna, enquiring of the obvious.

Yes madame, surely you knew that? replied the duke with a slight chuckle of amusement.

Of course I did, and what are your views on the attempts by the great assembly to pressure the triumvirate to take a more friendly stance on the affairs of the Elseyr Defense Union? she continued.

It is a noble cause to bring peace, and I doubt your religious titlings of the hochdeutsche state is really to do much of a stir, you have been listening too much to the preacher Stoljn, replied the duke, mildly annoyed at the persistence of the young woman. 

Ah to hell with your opinions about Stoljn, he is merely seeking out the best way forward for Rosenmarkke, a man is permitted some criticism, no? replied Radovna with a light laugh. 

Yes but such a man who raises crowds into a frenzy is not a man to be admired, surely your catholic upbringing shouldve taught you that, replied the duke.

Ah, well, here comes the hors douvers now, I shall be off, stated Radovna slightly miffed and not wishing to engage with the duke further, who also felt the same.
